shared_capability: A single reusable dataset freshness check, with staleness thresholds set as policy configuration, that reports per-dataset status (including 'unknown' for never-measured datasets) and can be consumed by dashboards, pre-review gates and grouped SLA reports.

distinct_needs.need: Know when the engine_test_runs dataset is stale, using a 60-minute threshold, before every hotfire review, so the dashboard does not silently show old test data.
A weekly ops-review SLA report on the freshness of the NCR tables, grouped by owner team, where a dataset that has never been measured is reported as 'unknown' and not as fresh.
One shared, reusable freshness capability to replace three hand-rolled per-engineer checks with differing thresholds, where thresholds are policy configuration rather than code.

symptoms.symptom: The hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine test data last week.
The BOM cost dashboard broke after an upstream column rename and nobody noticed for days.
No SLA view of NCR table freshness exists for the weekly ops review; the request insists unmeasured datasets must not look fresh.
Three forward deployed engineers each built their own freshness checks with different thresholds.

underlying_problem: Dataset staleness and schema changes are not monitored by any shared, policy-driven mechanism. Each team builds ad hoc checks, or none, so stale or changed data reaches reviews and dashboards before anyone notices, and unmeasured datasets have no defined status.
observed_facts: syn-req-001: The hotfire review dashboard silently showed three-day-old engine test data last week.
syn-req-001: The requester wants to know when engine_test_runs is stale, with a 60-minute threshold, before every review.
syn-req-002: The BOM cost dashboard broke when an upstream column was renamed and nobody noticed for days.
syn-req-002: The requester wants a check that compares each table schema against its declared contract and reports drift by field.
syn-req-003: The requester needs an SLA report on freshness of NCR tables for the weekly ops review, grouped by owner team.
syn-req-003: If a dataset has never been measured it must say unknown, not look fresh.
syn-req-004: Three forward deployed engineers each hand-rolled their own dataset freshness checks with different thresholds.
syn-req-004: The requester wants one shared, reusable capability where thresholds are policy configuration, not code.
interpretations: INFERENCE: syn-req-001, syn-req-003 and syn-req-004 all depend on measuring how old a dataset is against a threshold, so they share one capability; syn-req-001 needs a pre-review gate, syn-req-003 a grouped report, and syn-req-004 a reusable library.

INFERENCE: syn-req-002 checks schema against a contract, not age against a threshold. It shares only the broader goal of catching silent data-health problems, so it is left out of the freshness capability. It could later sit on the same monitoring substrate as a sibling capability.
INFERENCE: The word 'silently' in syn-req-001 and 'nobody noticed' in syn-req-002 point to a missing alerting or status signal rather than missing data.
INFERENCE: The 'unknown' rule in syn-req-003 is a design requirement that should also hold for syn-req-001 and syn-req-004. A dataset with no measurement must not pass a freshness check.
INFERENCE: Per-dataset thresholds, such as the 60-minute value for engine_test_runs, are likely policy data rather than code, which matches syn-req-004.
unknowns: Which datasets are in scope: only engine_test_runs and the NCR tables are named; no complete list is given.
What signal defines 'freshness' (a last-loaded timestamp, a source-system timestamp, or a row-count change) is not stated in any request.
Who owns the shared capability and the threshold policy is not stated.
Whether a stale result should block the review, raise an alert, or only display a status is not stated.
Where owner-team mapping for the SLA grouping comes from is not stated.
Whether the existing hand-rolled checks from syn-req-004 use thresholds that must be preserved during migration is not stated.
Whether syn-req-002 should be folded into this capability or kept as a separate schema-contract capability is not stated and needs a decision.
How often freshness must be measured (scheduled interval) is not stated; syn-req-001 requires a check before every review.
